overview: The City Council received a COVID-19 health update, approved a proclamation honoring the Board of Health, granted a catering license, and appointed a new member to the Hormel Commission. Councilors also discussed water and sewer base rate accounting during public participation and considered a resolution regarding road resurfacing priorities in the draft capital plan.

items.title: Board of Health COVID-19 Update
items.summary: Board of Health Director MaryAnn O'Connor provided an update on falling COVID-19 case counts, local vaccination distribution efforts, and the city's application for a regional vaccination site.

items.title: Board of Health COVID-19 Response Proclamation and Commendation
items.summary: The Council approved a joint mayoral proclamation and council commendation honoring Board of Health Director MaryAnn O'Connor, department staff, and volunteers for their service during the pandemic.

items.title: Catering License Application for Cafe Services
items.summary: The Council approved a catering license for Cafe Services to operate a corporate cafe at One Cabot Road.

items.title: Public Participation on Water and Sewer Base Charges
items.summary: Resident Robert Penta addressed the Council regarding the accounting procedures and revenue usage associated with water and sewer base fees enacted in 2017.

items.title: Appointment to the Hormel Commission
items.summary: The Council voted to appoint Brian Collins to serve as a member of the Hormel Commission.

items.title: Resolution on Capital Improvement Plan Road Resurfacing Priorities
items.summary: Vice President Knight introduced a resolution requesting that the administration revise the draft capital plan to prioritize resurfacing at least 10 miles of roadway per year along with revitalizing Medford Square and Mystic Avenue.
